Measurement to DLV/IAAF/AIMS standards, online registration, parking at Hauptschule Nord, disclaimer of liability, certificates via www.timeteam-jung.de

name: BW Forstsportlauf im Naturpark Schönbuch
description: The BW Forest Sports Run in Schönbuch Nature Park is an exciting running event set in the park’s picturesque surroundings. Organized by Forstsportverein Baden-Württemberg e.V., the event gives runners of all levels the opportunity to experience nature and the forest in a sporting atmosphere. The race features varied terrain in the forest and invites both recreational and competitive runners to discover the beauty of Schönbuch. Further details about registration and the event schedule are available on the club’s website.
course_highlights: Run through Schönbuch Nature Park in Tübingen
Varied forest terrain
Event for runners of all levels
additional: Several events in the forest sports calendar, with registration and accommodation information available. Scheduled for October 2026.

name: Friedrichstaler Waldlauf
description: The Friedrichstal Forest Run is part of the Stutensee Cup and will be held for the 11th time in 2026. The event comprises four scoring races over 10 km. Runners are automatically included in the standings if they take part in at least three races. The course offers an attractive running opportunity in autumnal Friedrichstal and welcomes runners of all ability levels. The five fastest runners will be honored after the final race on October 25, 2026. The event is organized by TV Friedrichstal 1899 e.V., the largest club in Stutensee.
course_highlights: Four scoring races over 10 km
Run through the autumnal Friedrichstal Forest
Take part in at least three races to qualify for the Stutensee Cup standings

Registration opens in September, nature experience, community event

description: The FSV Run takes place on October 25, 2026, in the Brucker Lache in Erlangen and offers races for all age groups, from Bambinis to adults. The course is a relatively flat 5 km loop, which runners complete twice for the 10 km race. Alongside the sporting experience, social engagement is also a focus: €2 per participant is donated to the Förderverein Erlanger Tafel. Children can enjoy medals and face painting, and free fruit, tea and non-alcoholic wheat beer are available in the finish area. The event also prioritizes environmental protection, for example by allowing participants to label and store their own bottles.

The 10 km race consists of two laps of the 5 km course
Course suitable for runners and Nordic walkers
additional: Late registrations are possible on the day of the event until 1 hour before the starts, for a €2 late-registration fee. The Bambini and schoolchildren’s races are free. The event supports the Förderverein Erlanger Tafel with donations per participant. name: Lauf um den Eisbrunn - 1. Lauf der Jedermannserie
location: Sportgelände des SV Mauren, Harburg, Donau-Ries, Bavaria, Germany
description: The Lauf um den Eisbrunn kicks off the LG Donau-Ries everyone’s running series in late autumn. The road race takes place in Harburg, with the start and finish at the SV Mauren sports grounds. Events include a main race of approximately 10 km, a 3 km short race, and a 7 km walking route. The event welcomes all running enthusiasts, from children to club runners, and offers a friendly atmosphere for individual entrants and series runners.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the SV Mauren sports grounds in Harburg
Main race of approx. 10 km, plus a 3 km short race and a 7 km walking route
Local late-autumn road race with typical October weather around 14 °C
additional: Race numbers with transponders are distributed on site before the start. The main race starts in the morning, followed by the shorter events. The series concludes with a final in Nördlingen on the third Sunday of Advent. A local race for all age groups, including children, teenagers, adults, and walkers. The series finale in Nördlingen offers community runners a good opportunity to prepare for winter.

name: Ohmbachsee Halbmarathon
location: Turn- und Festhalle Brücken, Brücken, Kusel, Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany
description: The Ohmbachsee Half Marathon is a long-standing race held annually at the picturesque Ohmbachsee in Brücken. The course passes through varied landscapes and offers runners an appealing mix of nature and sporting challenge. The event is organized by Laufgemeinschaft Ohmbachsee e.V. and is open to runners of all ability levels. The race starts at the Turn- und Festhalle Brücken, which also serves as the central meeting point.
course_highlights: Run along the picturesque Ohmbachsee
Varied natural course with forest and lakeside sections
Start and finish at the Turn- und Festhalle Brücken
additional: The race takes place on 25 October 2026, starting at 10:00 a.m. at the Turn- und Festhalle Brücken. The course is approximately 21 km long and runs from Dellstraße to the Ohmbachsee. Registration is available online and on site. The event is scheduled to take place in all weather conditions and has an established place in the regional running scene.

name: Pfinztallauf
description: The Pfinztal Run is a traditional event held annually at Hopfenberg Stadium in Pfinztal. The course runs through the idyllic countryside along the Pfinz, passing Söllingen and Kleinsteinbach, with a turnaround point in Kleinsteinbach. The event offers various distances for all age groups, from Bambini and schoolchildren’s races to 10 km runs. After finishing in the stadium, participants can enjoy a warm atmosphere with an awards ceremony, trophies, medals, and a large cake buffet in the TSV hall.
course_highlights: The route runs through Pfinztal and along a scenic section of the Pfinz
Turnaround point at the Kleinsteinbach festival grounds
Finish at Hopfenberg Stadium, with a stadium announcer
additional: Start times: 09:30 for the 3 km school team race and 5 km run, 10:00 for the 10 km run, and from 11:15 for the Bambini and schoolchildren’s races. The course partly follows cycle paths and roads, including railway underpasses. After the race, there is a large cake buffet and an awards ceremony with trophies, medals, and certificates in the TSV hall. The event offers a range of distances, including school and youth competitions, with refreshments and an awards ceremony at Hopfenberg Stadium.

name: Porzellinerlauf
location: Sportplatz Am Dohlenstein, Kahla, Thüringen, Germany
description: The Porzellinerlauf Kahla is a traditional autumn road race starting and finishing at the Am Dohlenstein sports ground in Kahla, Thuringia. The 13 km race is the main event, alongside shorter children’s and youth races, making the day appealing to both families and regular runners. Organised by SV 1910 Kahla e.V. since 1971, the race combines a sporting challenge with the local porcelain tradition. Regional timekeepers oversee the course, which receives particularly positive feedback for its route.
course_highlights: Start and finish at the Am Dohlenstein sports ground
13 km main race, with shorter children’s and youth races
Route through Kahla with a connection to its porcelain tradition
additional: The field is modest, with around 101 to 300 runners and more than one hundred finishers in recent editions. Typical November weather in Kahla is around 7 °C, with frequent rain. Timing is provided by regional timekeepers. The race has been established since 1971 and regularly attracts between 101 and 300 participants. The course is known for its good condition and attractive surroundings. The event also includes refreshments, showers and an awards ceremony.

name: VR Bank Westküsten Herbstlauf Schafstedt
description: The VR Bank Westküsten Autumn Run Schafstedt is an autumn running event in Schafstedt, Schleswig-Holstein, taking place for the 38th time in 2026. Distances include 3 km, 5 km and 10 km runs, as well as a 5 km walking route. The event welcomes adults and younger participants and fosters a family-friendly atmosphere with children’s and youth races. The routes pass through the autumn landscape in the fresh air and offer an alternative to city runs.
course_highlights: The 3 km route is flat
The 5 km run and 5 km walk include some hills
All races finish at the same finish line
additional: Children’s and youth races are part of the event. Typical October weather in Schafstedt is around 14 °C during the day and 6 °C at night, mostly cloudy, with an average of 40 mm of precipitation. The event also includes walking options and is aimed at families and young people. October weather is generally mild, with temperatures around 6–14 °C, creating ideal conditions for an autumn run.

name: Thüngersheimer Bocksbeutellauf 2026
description: The Thüngersheim Bocksbeutel Run is a traditional race held annually in Thüngersheim. The event offers runners of all ages a friendly, welcoming atmosphere, with a generous runners’ buffet, a large cake and coffee bar, and a medal and bottle of wine for every finisher. Children receive a small gift. The race is a celebration of the local running community, combining sporting ambition with a sociable gathering.
course_highlights: Run through the picturesque wine region around Thüngersheim
Generous runners’ buffet and large cake and coffee bar
A bottle of wine for every finisher, or a gift for children
additional: Every finisher receives a medal and a bottle of wine; children receive a small gift. A generous runners’ buffet and a large cake and coffee bar are available. Registration is open until 14.09.2026 to benefit from lower fees. Distances: 600 m, 2.5 km, 5 km, 10 km; date: 25 October 2026; local race, family- and club-friendly

name: Freisinger Strassenlauf pwd. by Munich Airport
24. Röntgenlauf
description: The Röntgenlauf in Remscheid is a traditional cross-country race with various distances, including 5 km, 10 km, half marathon, marathon and ultramarathon. The half marathon is especially popular, attracting up to 1,500 participants, and is considered one of Germany’s largest cross-country races. The routes pass through varied natural scenery, with forest trails and paved sections; the half marathon covers about one third of the Röntgenweg. A shuttle service takes half marathon participants from the finish back to the start. The event also places emphasis on environmental protection by recommending reusable drinking cups.
course_highlights: 5 km and 10 km races on a loop between Hackenberg and Wuppersperre, with approximately 95 m and 190 m of elevation gain, respectively
Half marathon with approximately 405 m of ascent and 560 m of descent; part of the ultramarathon route
Route along forest trails and paved sections; not suitable for spiked shoes
additional: The half marathon has a minimum age of 16; the marathon and ultramarathon have a minimum age of 18. Minors need written consent from a parent or guardian. There is a clothing transport service from the start to the finish and a bus transfer from the finish back to the start. Participants are asked to bring their own reusable drinking cups to help protect the environment. The entry fee includes a race bib, finisher’s medal and refreshments. Distances range from 5 km to the ultramarathon (63.3 km), including children’s races and cross-country races; registration is open until 25 October 2026.

name: 26. Dresden-Marathon / DRESDEN-MARATHON
description: The DRESDEN-MARATHON has been held regularly in late October since 1999. It offers a flat, fast course through the Saxon state capital, passing its famous sights. The route goes through the historic Old Town, including Brühl’s Terrace, the Semper Opera House and other Baroque buildings, as well as the lively Neustadt district. More than 300 musicians and numerous bands create a special atmosphere along the course. The second half of the marathon runs through the Blasewitz district, with views of the palaces on the Loschwitz Elbe slope and the villas along Goetheallee, before returning to the Old Town along the Elbe.
course_highlights: Flat, fast course through Dresden’s historic Old Town and Neustadt district
Illuminated Waldschlößchen Tunnel and bridge, and the Großer Garten
Atmosphere created by more than 300 musicians and bands along the course
additional: More than 300 musicians and numerous bands create an atmosphere along the course. There is a marathon expo, race-pack collection and a SPARKASSEN pacemaker service. After the race, medal engraving, a photo service, showers, changing rooms and toilets, as well as award ceremonies, are available. The evening before the race, an anniversary party takes place in the marquee behind Heinz Steyer Stadium (€25 admission; limited capacity). Several race distances, online registration, health questionnaire, event on 24 and 25 October 2026

name: Frankenwaldlauf um den Preis der Kulmbacher Brauerei
description: The Frankenwald Run for the Kulmbacher Brewery Prize is a relaxed running event in the beautiful Franconian Forest village of Ludwigschorgast, organised by runners for runners. Featuring a 1.5-kilometre singletrack trail as an exciting alternative to the paved section, the event welcomes both ambitious runners and recreational athletes, with a fun run and Nordic walking. Alongside sporting ambition, the focus is on having fun amid the Franconian Forest’s romantically rugged natural scenery. The overall male and female winners of the main race receive prize money, and the club with the most participants receives a financial award.
course_highlights: A 1.5 km singletrack trail replaces the paved section from Wirsberg to the Goldener Adler Hut
Run through the Franconian Forest’s romantically rugged natural scenery
A variety of events: main race, fun run (5 km) and Nordic walking (8.4 km)
additional: Late registration is available on the event day at the FC Ludwigschorgast sports hall from 12:30 to 13:30, for an additional fee of 5 euros. All participants receive a small gift from Kulmbacher when they hand in their race number at the finish. Tea, non-alcoholic drinks, biscuits, pretzel sticks and gummy bears are available at the finish. The race number must be worn clearly visible on the front of the body; otherwise, participants will be disqualified. There is a team competition in the main race, with non-cash prizes and a challenge trophy for the fastest men’s team. Courses in the Franconian Forest region; registration opens on 18 September; late registration at the start for a fee; refreshments at the finish; start at 9:00; awards ceremony at 11:30.

name: Mainova Frankfurt Marathon
description: The Mainova Frankfurt Marathon is a special running experience, with a fast course, fantastic support from the crowds along the route and an overwhelming finish. The event offers a varied program for the whole running family, including the classic marathon, relay marathon, mini-marathon and Struwwelpeter Run for children. The marathon covers the full distance of 42.195 kilometers through Frankfurt and is known for its wonderful atmosphere and the street festival surrounding the event.

Fantastic support from the crowds along the route
Finish in the magnificently illuminated Festhalle

There is an extensive supporting program featuring a marathon expo, Pasta Party, pretzel run and course-side festivals. The pretzel run takes place the day before. The children's races (Mini-Marathon and Struwwelpeter Run) also finish in the Festhalle. The event is part of a large street festival in Frankfurt. Road race, registration, program for the running family, Green Marathon, Pasta Party, course-side festivals

The main event is a flat 10 km race for adults, which starts in the morning. There is also a 5 km youth race and several 1.1 km children’s races, divided by age and gender. description: The Drachenlauf is a challenging trail race in the Siebengebirge near Königswinter, taking place on October 25, 2026. The route passes through one of Germany’s oldest nature parks and features technically demanding trails with more than a thousand metres of elevation gain, steep climbs and long descents. The race is for experienced runners who want to experience nature and test their limits. The event has a distinctive atmosphere in the autumn forest of the Rhenish Alps and fosters a sense of community among participants.

Autumn scenery in the Rhenish Alps

On-site late registration is possible if places are still available, for a fee of 4 euros. Participants taking part for the 10th, 15th or 20th time receive special All-Timer shirts and race numbers. Shuttle buses run from the largest car park (REWE car park) to the start. The awards ceremony takes place at around 2 p.m. at Heinrich-Imbusch-Haus. The event invites runners to take part in this special event with a headlamp and a pumpkin grin. The race is flexible, allowing each participant to choose their own start location and time. After the run, results can be uploaded online and a certificate can be downloaded for printing. Participants can also order a medal and a race shirt to commemorate the experience.
course_highlights: Virtual race with a flexible start location and time

Upload results online and download a certificate to print

A digital starting signal is given on social media. Medals and shirts can be ordered separately. name: Halloween-Run-Bremen
description: The Halloween Run Bremen 2026 takes place on October 31 and offers runners a spooky race experience around Werdersee. With five different distances, from 1 km to the 42.195 km marathon, there is something for every ability level. The courses are measured in accordance with German Athletics Association rules and are eligible for record lists, underscoring the competitive nature of the event. Alongside the sporting event, participants can look forward to a spooky atmosphere with costumes, lights and fog, as well as an awards ceremony and a closing fireworks display.

Start and finish area at Werdersee, between the Finnbahn and the barbecue area

A spectacular fireworks display at 18:00 rounds off the event. There are also relay competitions for the marathon (5-person relay). The race bib with RFID chip serves as the relay baton and must be brought by the team. Costumes are expressly encouraged but are not compulsory. Participants can register online. There are various distances and relay options; the event takes place at night and offers a spooky atmosphere.

name: 34. Mündener Altstadtlauf
description: The 34th Mündener Altstadtlauf takes place on October 31, 2026, in Hann. Münden and offers suitable distances for runners of different age groups and ability levels. The event includes Bambini and schoolchildren’s races, as well as 5 km and 10 km races for recreational and competitive runners. The course is measured by the Lower Saxony Athletics Association and is therefore eligible for record times. In addition to individual rankings, there are group and team rankings, making the race particularly appealing to teams. The organizing team places great importance on professional delivery and continually improving the event.

5 km course with a group ranking and 10 km course with a team ranking (at least one woman per team)

Around 40 volunteers help with setup and dismantling and secure the race routes. Various local institutions, including the fire department, police, and city administration, are involved. name: 6. Halloween Run

The courses are measured in accordance with German Athletics Association rules and are eligible for record lists, underscoring the competitive nature of the event. Alongside the sporting event, participants can look forward to a spooky atmosphere with costumes, lights and fog, as well as a spectacular fireworks display to close the event. The event is open to all age groups and ability levels, and includes relay races and a children’s run.

The start and finish area is between the Finnbahn at Werdersee and the Grillwiese/DLRG lifeguard station. Several running distances, including the marathon, take place on measured loops; costumes are encouraged; the event concludes with fireworks.

name: Bredstedt-Cross
description: The 39th Bredstedt Cross takes place on 31 October 2026 at Sportpark Bredstedt and is hosted by Bredstedter TSV. The event offers cross-country races for a wide range of ages, from children and young people to senior competitors and numerous masters categories. There are short and long cross-country races for men and women, as well as separate age categories from M6/W6 to M75/W75, including youth and U18/U20. The event is listed as category 6.5.1, an event held away from a stadium, and offers a varied competition format for all age groups.

name: Kreismeisterschaft und 3. Halloween-Crosslauf im Örtzetal zu Munster

Distances range from 500 metres to 10 kilometres, offering a local, club-oriented atmosphere rather than the feel of a major city race. The race takes place in the autumnal Örtzetal region and is a popular seasonal event organised by Eintracht Munster.

name: Köstritzer Parklauf
location: Köstritzer Park, Bad Köstritz, Thuringia, Germany

The event offers short races for children and young people, as well as longer distances for adults and masters, from 500 m to the 12 km main race. It attracts numerous local and regional clubs, mainly from Thuringia, but also from Saxony and Bavaria. The 27th edition of the race is known for its strong regional turnout.

A range of distances from 500 m to 12 km

The event includes races for children and young people, as well as main races for adults and masters. name: Nordhessische Crosslaufmeisterschaften
description: The North Hesse Cross-Country Championships are a regional club and regional cross-country championship held in various locations across North Hesse. The races take place on cross-country terrain, not on closed roads, and are organized by various athletics districts and clubs.

The event offers various distances and levels of difficulty suitable for all age groups and ability levels.

name: 19. Bothfelder Waldlauf

The race is part of the Hannover Region Running Pass and offers changing and shower facilities in the finish area. Affordable food, drinks, and free hot tea are available. The event is open to runners of all age groups, including Bambinis, with short-distance races.

Forest trails and well-maintained forest roads
Start and finish at the Bothfeld district sports ground

The children’s race award ceremonies take place approximately 60 minutes after the races; ceremonies for the longer races follow immediately after the finish. Public transport is available via tram line 13, and parking is available nearby. The registration deadline is October 30, 2026; the event takes place in typical November weather in Hanover; the event is outside the official stadium calendar.

name: 28. Tangerpokallauf
description: The 28th Tanger Cup Run in Demker is the oldest running event organized by SC Demker '95 and is part of the Elbe-Ohre Cup. The course runs through the autumnal Tanger lowlands between Demker and Weißewarte, past Deutsches Eck, under the Stendal–Magdeburg railway line, and through the Süppling woodland. Distances offered are 1.2 km for children and young people, and 5.4 km and 12.0 km for older young people and adults. The terrain is mostly flat, with gentle rises formed by the dikes surrounding Demker.
course_highlights: Flat course through the Tanger lowlands between Demker and Weißewarte
Runs along the Tanger and past Deutsches Eck
Passes through the Süppling woodland
additional: Distances: 1.2 km (children/young people), 5.4 km and 12.0 km (older young people/adults). The terrain is flat throughout, with the dikes as the only rises. The course passes under the Stendal–Magdeburg railway line. The event takes place on November 1, 2026. Information is also provided about registration, results, photos, and accommodation in Demker.

name: Käppelelauf 2026
description: The Käppelelauf is a long-standing running event held every year on November 1 in Reudern near Nürtingen. The course covers 8.7 kilometers with around 245 meters of elevation gain on gravel forest paths, climbing to the Käppele parking area. The race is part of the TSV Beuren Tälescup race series and also offers a separate Nordic walking category. After the race, there is an awards ceremony and a traditional buffet, making the event a social occasion.
course_highlights: 8.7-kilometer course with approx. 245 meters of elevation gain
Route on gravel forest paths
Finish at the Käppele parking area
additional: Start at the edge of the forest in Reudern; a lead bicycle rides ahead of the first woman and first man. Awards ceremony and traditional buffet after the race; separate category for Nordic walkers; part of the TSV Beuren Tälescup race series. Start at 10 a.m. at the Reudern sports ground. Registration in advance only. November weather is usually rainy, with temperatures around 2–7°C.

name: LG Alsternord Herbstwaldlauf 2026
description: The LG Alsternord Autumn Forest Run is a local autumn race through the forest in Norderstedt, north of Hamburg. Organized by LG Alsternord Hamburg e.V., the race starts at 11:00 a.m. at the Rantzauer Forst-Thingplatz. Participants can choose between 5 km and 10 km routes, including a cross-country option. The race takes place away from city streets in the Rantzauer Forst area and also offers walking and hiking events. With a modest field of usually 101 to 300 runners, the event has more of a club-run feel than that of a major race.
course_highlights: Run through the autumnal Rantzauer Forst, away from city streets
5 km, 10 km and cross-country options
Modest field with a club-run atmosphere
additional: Results are published via race result; public start lists, photos, reports and historical rankings are available. In addition to the races, there are walking and hiking events, including a 5 km walk. Typical November weather is around 7 °C, with rainy days. The event takes place in typical November weather, around 7°C and with rainy conditions. It is open to runners and walkers of all ages, with a modest participant count of between 101 and 300.

name: Neustädter Sparkassen Nachtlauf
location: Neustadt an der Aisch, Neustadt an der Aisch, Bavaria, Germany
organizer: Turn- und Sportverein 1861/08 Neustadt an der Aisch e.V.
description: The Sparkassen Night Run in Neustadt an der Aisch is a popular running event with several competitions, including a children’s run, fun run, Nordic walking and the main race. The event takes place in the town centre, with the start and finish at the town hall on the market square. It offers an attractive course that has been adapted to participants’ needs. Race numbers are available at the town hall, and showers and changing rooms are available at the TSV sports ground. The award ceremonies take place in the evening in front of the Sparkasse or at the town hall. Every participant receives a small thank-you bag at the finish.
course_highlights: The course runs through the town centre, with adjustments to avoid narrow sections
Start and finish at the town hall on the market square
Showers and changing rooms available at the TSV sports ground
additional: Late entries are accepted at the town hall until 30 minutes before the respective start, for a late-entry fee of 2€. Race-number distribution starts at 15:45 at the town hall. Jackets may be left at the town hall or in the Stadtwerke tent during the race, at the owner's own risk. For safety reasons, children start in staggered groups: boys 3 minutes before girls. Main-race prize money: 1st place 150€, 2nd place 100€, 3rd place 75€. Course changes are possible. Children’s-run course length: 1.7 km; main race: 4 laps; fun run: 2 laps. The event takes place in the town of Neustadt an der Aisch, with the start and finish near the Neustadthalle and at the town hall on the market square.

name: Tiergarten-Cross
description: The Tiergarten Cross in Schleswig is a local cross-country race taking place on November 1, 2026. The event offers two main distances, 4.4 km and 8.8 km, which start one after the other so the fields are separate. The course is undulating and demands constant changes of pace, making the race varied. In addition to the main races, there are also children’s and youth races, making the event family-friendly and diverse.
course_highlights: Finishes in Tiergarten Schleswig, the most distinctive point on the course
Undulating course with constant small changes of pace
Separate start times for the 4.4 km and 8.8 km distances
additional: The event also includes children’s and youth races. Typical November weather in Schleswig is cool, with daytime highs of around 7 °C, and rainy on most days. The event takes place in Tiergarten Schleswig, is weather-dependent (November is usually rainy), and offers a family-friendly atmosphere with various race categories.

name: Winterlaufserie 2026/2027, 1. Wertungslauf
description: The Winter Run Series in Hamm is a long-standing winter road-running series, now taking place for the 51st time. The first scoring race covers a distance of 15 km on roads outside the stadium. The event attracts many club runners from Westphalia and beyond, including teams from Dortmund, Münster and Bielefeld. The race offers a challenging course in the cool November weather and is a popular start to the winter season for runners of all abilities.
course_highlights: 15 km road race outside the stadium
A field with a strong club-running presence from Westphalia and the surrounding area
Typically cool and rainy November weather
additional: The starting location is Ahnatal. The average November temperature is around 7°C, with frequent rain (approximately 45 mm of precipitation). The event is part of the Winter Run Series, which may take place in typical weather of around 7°C with rain. It is the series’ first scoring race and appeals to runners from various regions.

name: Stadtparkstaffelmarathon
description:
